column1: # Game profile of Assassin's Creed: The Rebel Collection (Switch, 1.0.0, the cartridge's base game): Black Flag and Rogue, Ubisoft's AnvilNext, NVN, SDK 8.2.0,
# Havok and Wwise. Two programs: this one (010044700DEB0000), whose launcher picks a game, and 010044700DEB0001 (not profiled). On the Mac this program boots
# through the launcher's parameter into Black Flag's menus and its opening at sea under control, at 30 fps. Its shaders are BNSH files of one stage each, 326 in main
# and 32,821 in the LZO1X blocks of the .forge archives (dm/gfx/tools/anvil_forge.py; see README.md)
# The provisional profile the survey made (dm/games/profile_guess.py), with the launcher's parameter added (launch_param)
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# The launcher (this program, started from HOME) restarts it with oe::ExecuteProgram(0, "/launcher:off /gamesoundlanguage:en /gamemenulanguage:en
# /gamerewardsPurchased:0") to start Black Flag; the host runs one program, so it hands that parameter over at the start instead (hle_oe.c), and the game
# starts Black Flag without the launcher. Rogue, the launcher's other choice, is program 1
# Every BNSH file holds one stage, in main and in the .forge archives, and the game draws with a vertex shader of one file and a pixel shader of another: every vertex shader is
# paired with the pixel shader cover (shader_split.py separable_pairs), so it is padded for any of them
